correctness.rationale: The degree-six neighbours give exactly the displayed triple inequality. A closed-walk bijection of the 64-state transfer automaton proves each finite-size formula, while exhaustive 512-triple component reduction shows only a 31-state primitive recurrent class at threshold four and a seven-state class plus all-zero loop at threshold five. Direct SymPy integer characteristic-polynomial checks yield degree-nine and cubic factors; rational Collatz inequalities and exact Sturm counts isolate the four-neighbour Perron root. Perron analytic perturbation and a variance-O(n) argument justify density convergence. Independent full-vertex occupation bitmask exhaustive tests for n=4,5,6 and independently computed gap-gas counts confirm the graph and transfer interpretations. The finite experiments are not asserted to prove the infinite conclusion.

originality.rationale: A direct comparison was made with three primary sources: Kogut–Leath (1981) describes bulk percolation simulations at the abstract level but full text is unavailable; Chang–Shrock (2000) covers exactly the triangular three-row toroidal graph but computes chromatic polynomials of proper colourings; Choi–Yu (2019) fully covers triangular bootstrap simulation/finite-size critical exponents but not a uniform fixed-point count. The closest earlier square three-row bootstrap-culling polynomial concerns fewer edges and a different threshold; a four-column witness is triangular stable and square unstable. Targeted published-record searches found no equivalent or dominating claim. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment with explicit residual full-text and indexing risks.
residual_risks: The 1981 original Kogut–Leath full text was not available; an appendix or unindexed finite-width enumeration could overlap despite its abstract describing bulk simulations.

value.rationale: The first nondegenerate three-row periodic triangular strip has six distinct neighbours per vertex and natural consecutive high culling thresholds four and five. The theorem shows not merely different counts but a sharp local-void geometry change: whole empty columns occur at positive density at threshold four but are entirely excluded by threshold five in any nonempty frozen state. The finite-width exact ninth-degree and cubic entropies, occupancy densities, and complete threshold-five vacancy-gas classification are motivated benchmarks for lattice bootstrap/stability research and are not consequences of a planar threshold or a simple hard-core formula alone.
